sentence: This project tests whether a stronger form of metformin, which gathers in cancer cells, can treat the most aggressive type of lung cancer.
This project develops proteins that try to renew aged thymic epithelial cells and help old mice make more T cells.
This project builds a low-cost camera that takes images of the retina of premature infants to screen for retinal diseases.
This project studies the causes of chronic lung diseases such as asthma by using quantitative data analysis methods.
This project uses sequencing methods to study how HIV changes over time and how it acts inside host cells.
This project studies how cardiac cells make a protein that helps the heart keep a proper rhythm.
This project offers a short course on how pancreatic cancer is diagnosed, treated and develops.
This project studies how immune cells and stromal cells around a prostate tumor help the cancer grow and respond to hormone therapy.
This project develops a cancer treatment that targets a specific protein involved in the growth of prostate cancer cells.
This project studies why tyrosine kinase inhibitors cause vascular dysfunction, using stem cells, engineered vascular tissues and animal models.
This project looks for chemical signatures that tell apart embryos with and without errors in the chemical tags on genes.
This project builds vaccines that use T cells to protect against antibiotic-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus.
This project tests whether an iron-based contrast agent on MRI and serum biomarkers can reveal early nerve degeneration after peripheral nerve injury.
This project provides genomics, bioinformatics and cell biology techniques for research on nutrition and metabolic conditions.
This project provides data management and data analysis for studies of how B cell and T cell responses develop and last in viral infection.
This project studies how pain lowers the release of acetylcholine in the brain circuits that control pain.
This project studies how the high sugar levels in diabetic urine make Group B Streptococcus more harmful and more resistant to immune defenses.
This project predicts brain networks linked to aggression and tests their role in aggressive and pro-social behavior, especially in females.
This project builds a microfluidic platform that traps bacteria from whole blood to test how they respond to antibiotics.
This project studies how abnormal activation of the complement pathway disrupts synapses in the early postnatal brain after pediatric brain injury.
